page: Amazon Web Services im4gn.xlarge is a storage-optimized instance powered by an ARM64 AWS Graviton processor using the Neoverse-N1 architecture. It features 4 dedicated physical cores running at 2.5 GHz with a single thread per core, paired with 16.0 GB of system memory. A primary characteristic of this instance is its bundled local storage, which provides 1875 GB of NVMe SSD capacity. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark results show average performance for standard compute tasks, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests scoring in the middle 50% tier. Memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks also performs at an average level, though small-block cached read bandwidth and single-threaded decompression tasks fall into the lower 10% to 25% performance brackets. The ARMv8 architecture includes hardware-accelerated AES cryptography but lacks x86-specific vector extensions such as AVX or AMX.

From a resource density perspective, the im4gn.xlarge offers a high ratio of local NVMe storage relative to its compute and memory allocation. This makes it a cost-efficient choice for workloads that require fast local read/write capabilities without needing massive CPU or memory resources. Appropriate workloads include local databases, caching layers, log indexing, and storage-intensive general-purpose applications.
